spec_fidelity: The hero now visibly suggests summoning and all required menu items remain, but the spirit is still an abstract diamond haze and the Grind card wraps onto a second row, weakening the intended hub navigation.
unity: The teal/gold ritual language is coherent, yet the separated two-row menu and large gap around the title fragment the vertical flow.
variety: Summon is appropriately dominant, but the three secondary cards have limited semantic identity and the hero lacks a memorable spirit silhouette.
conflict: A more distinctive hero and menu differentiation should stay inside the same occult geometry and restrained palette.
resolution: Use one ritual-seal language throughout, introduce semantic variation through silhouette, icon, and scale, and restore a deliberate single-row navigation structure.
moderator_revision: Develop the hero into a readable ethereal spirit silhouette—head, shoulders or wings emerging within the existing concentric seal—while keeping the teal haze, gold glyphs, and fine-line geometry. Tighten the title directly beneath the hero and place all four menu destinations in one aligned row across the lower area. Keep Summon wider and gold-emphasized as the primary action; give Roster, Battle, and Grind distinct but restrained icons and equal secondary card dimensions. Reduce unused vertical gaps so hero, title, and navigation read as one unified hub.
